question: Assume today is 2026-09-08. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total number of A&E attendances in England in September 2026 (all A&E types, including minor injury units and walk-in centres), as reported in NHS England's monthly A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions statistics.

target.what: Total number of A&E attendances (all A&E types, including major A&E departments, single-specialty A&E, minor injury units and walk-in centres) in England during September 2026, as reported in NHS England's monthly A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions statistics (the 'A&E attendances' count, i.e.
target.publisher: NHS England (A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions monthly statistics)
target.caveats: Target period is future/ongoing relative to the 2026-09-08 cutoff, so no published value exists; must be forecast. Working interpretation: all A&E types combined (type 1 major, type 2 single-specialty, type 3 minor injury units/walk-in centres, plus any type 4/other as classified), England only, att

candidates.perspective: NHS England published monthly A&E series
candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 attendances will follow the level and seasonal pattern of recent Septembers and the trailing 12 months; the most recent published months before cutoff (through ~June/July 2026) anchor the level, and a September seasonal factor (September vs summer/adjacent months) scales it. Direction: September typically slightly above August/July.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly all-A&E-type attendance totals for England for each month from Jan 2023 through the latest month published before 2026-09-08 (ideally June or July 2026); plus September values for 2023, 2024, 2025 to derive a September seasonal ratio vs the preceding months. Minimum: latest 3-6 months of all-type totals and at least two prior Septembers.

p61.role: Total all-type A&E attendances in England, July 2026 (latest observed monthly level)

a1.role: Seasonal ratio of September 2026 to July 2026 total attendances

methods.rationale: Anchors on the latest observed monthly total (July 2026, p61) and applies a modest September/July seasonal ratio. Shared dependency: relies on the July 2026 NHS England figure being accurate and on the seasonal ratio assumption; failure mode is an unusual September surge or dip.

p63.role: Total all-type A&E attendances in England over the 12 months to July 2026 (annual level)

a2.role: Year-on-year growth factor for September 2026 vs September 2025

methods.rationale: Uses the 12-month cumulative total (p63) divided by 12 as a smoothed annual monthly level, then applies a year-on-year growth factor consistent with the +2.1% (April) and +3.3% (July) growth observed. Shared dependency: p63 overlaps with p61 in the same NHS England series; failure mode is that the 12-month average understates the summer peak, so the growth factor must carry the seasonal uplift.

p37.role: Average daily all-type A&E attendances in England, June 2026

a1.role: Seasonal ratio of September 2026 to the June/July summer level

methods.rationale: Builds a monthly total from the June 2026 daily average (p37) times the number of days in September, with the same seasonal ratio. Shared dependency: p37 and p61 are both summer 2026 NHS England levels; failure mode is that June's daily rate may differ from September's.

assumptions.name: September 2026 vs July 2026 seasonal ratio
assumptions.rationale: September typically sits close to the July/August summer level, with a small upward drift as respiratory season begins; the July 2026 level (p61) is the latest observed month, so a ratio near 1 with modest spread is used. No kept point gives the exact September/July ratio, so this is an explicit seasonal transfer factor.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 follows the recent summer level without a major disruption.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 attendances were materially above or below the July 2026 level (e.g. an August/September 2026 published total).

assumptions.name: September 2026 vs September 2025 year-on-year growth factor
assumptions.rationale: Recent total attendance growth was +2.1% in April 2026 (p2) and +3.3% in July 2026 (p62); a factor near 1.03 continues that trend into September 2026.
assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 growth trend continues into September.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published September 2026 total showing growth well outside 0-7% year-on-year.

p323.role: Total all-type A&E attendances in England, September 2025

a3.role: Year-on-year growth factor for September 2026 vs September 2025

methods.rationale: Direct seasonal route: observed September 2025 total (p323) scaled by the 2026 YoY growth factor. assumptions.name: September 2026 vs July 2026 seasonal ratio
assumptions.rationale: September typically sits close to the late-summer level; recent Septembers (2023, 2025) were near or slightly above the preceding July/August. A symmetric range around 1.0 reflects uncertainty in the seasonal step.
assumptions.applies_when: The July 2026 level is a valid anchor for the late-summer plateau and September does not deviate sharply.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 is materially above or below the July 2026 level (e.g. a published August/September figure).

assumptions.name: September 2026 vs September 2025 year-on-year growth factor
assumptions.rationale: Recent YoY growth has been 2.1% (April 2026) to 3.3% (July 2026); a central 3% with a range spanning those observations is consistent with the kept growth evidence.
assumptions.applies_when: The recent growth regime continues into September 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published September 2026 figure showing growth outside the 0-7% range.

assumptions.name: September 2026 vs September 2025 year-on-year growth factor (September-anchored route)
assumptions.rationale: Same growth regime as a2 but applied to the observed September 2025 total (p323) rather than the 12-month average; central 3% spans the 2.1% April and 3.3% July 2026 YoY observations.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2025 is a valid base and the 2026 growth regime continues.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published September 2026 figure showing growth outside 0-7%.

methods.label: m1

p61.role: Total all-type A&E attendances in England, July 2026 (latest observed monthly level)

a1.role: Seasonal ratio of September 2026 to July 2026 total attendances

methods.rationale: Anchors on the latest observed monthly total (July 2026, p61) and applies a September-to-July seasonal ratio. Shared dependency: relies on the July 2026 level being representative of the late-summer plateau; failure mode is an unusual September surge or dip.
methods.error: input p61: id p61 unknown or discarded

methods.label: m2

p63.role: Total all-type A&E attendances in England over the 12 months to July 2026 (annual level)

a2.role: Year-on-year growth factor for September 2026 vs September 2025

methods.rationale: Uses the 12-month cumulative to July 2026 (p63) as the annual level, converts to a monthly average, and applies a YoY growth factor. Shared dependency: the annual average may understate the September level if September is seasonally above average; failure mode is a growth regime shift.
methods.error: input p63: id p63 unknown or discarded

methods.label: m3

p37.role: Average daily all-type A&E attendances in England, June 2026

a1.role: Seasonal ratio of September 2026 to the June/July summer level

methods.rationale: Uses the June 2026 daily average (p37), scales to 30 days, and applies the seasonal ratio. Shared dependency with m1 on the summer level; failure mode is that June's daily average may not represent the September plateau.
methods.error: input p37: id p37 unknown or discarded

methods.label: m4

p323.role: Total all-type A&E attendances in England, September 2025

a3.role: Year-on-year growth factor for September 2026 vs September 2025

methods.rationale: Direct seasonal route: observed September 2025 total (p323) scaled by the 2026 YoY growth factor. This is the cleanest route because it uses the same calendar month; failure mode is that p323 is rounded to 2.31m and the 2026 growth regime may differ from the 2-3% observed in spring/summer.
methods.error: input p323: id p323 unknown or discarded

kept.name: September 2026 vs July 2026 seasonal ratio
kept.rationale: September typically sits close to the late-summer level; recent Septembers (2023, 2025) were near or slightly above the preceding July/August. A symmetric range around 1.0 reflects uncertainty in the seasonal step.
kept.applies_when: The July 2026 level is a valid anchor for the late-summer plateau and September does not deviate sharply.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 is materially above or below the July 2026 level (e.g. a published August/September figure).

kept.name: September 2026 vs September 2025 year-on-year growth factor
kept.rationale: Recent YoY growth has been 2.1% (April 2026) to 3.3% (July 2026); a central 3% with a range spanning those observations is consistent with the kept growth evidence.
kept.applies_when: The recent growth regime continues into September 2026.
kept.falsified_by: A published September 2026 figure showing growth outside the 0-7% range.

kept.name: September 2026 vs September 2025 year-on-year growth factor (September-anchored route)
kept.rationale: Same growth regime as a2 but applied to the observed September 2025 total (p323) rather than the 12-month average; central 3% spans the 2.1% April and 3.3% July 2026 YoY observations.
kept.applies_when: September 2025 is a valid base and the 2026 growth regime continues.
kept.falsified_by: A published September 2026 figure showing growth outside 0-7%.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
